reviews.body:
**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED.** One blocking item: a rollback recipe in this repo's docs that v2.5.0 makes unsafe. Everything else in the bump checks out (below). Fixing it is a docs-only push on this branch. The chart, the pins and the rebuilt templates need no change.

## Upstream

appVersion: v2.3.0 → v2.5.0
chart 0.9.3 → 0.10.4, app v2.3.0 → v2.5.0 (computed from the vendored `Chart.yaml` at base and head; there is no chart index, the chart is built from the git tag). Renovate labels this a *minor*, but `.github/renovate-global.json` routes a Garage minor to `major`, un-armed. The operator turned on auto-merge at 13:41Z, so this APPROVED-or-not decides the merge.

Releases crossed: **v2.4.0** (2026-09-06), **v2.4.1** (2026-09-08), **v2.5.0** (2026-10-24).

- **v2.4.0**: "no breaking changes when migrating from v2.3.0". ⚠ **It panics on start with Kubernetes discovery** (#1526). This deployment uses k8s discovery (garagenodes CRD + ClusterRole), so v2.4.0 would have crash-looped. **v2.4.1** fixes it (#1416/#1473/#1526–#1528), and v2.5.0 carries the fix. Jumping straight to v2.5.0 is correct. Never pin v2.4.0 here.
- **v2.5.0, breaking 1 — no downgrade.** Upstream, verbatim: *"once a node is upgraded, you must not downgrade it back to older Garage versions. You can still mix-and-match nodes running older and newer versions of the v2.x branch within a cluster."* Mixed versions during the zone-by-zone roll are therefore fine. **A revert is not.** → BLOCKING finding below.
- **v2.5.0, breaking 2 — `(Put|Get|Delete)BucketLifecycle` now needs owner permission** (#1573, security). This repo makes no lifecycle calls (grepped `*.tf/*.sh/*.yaml/*.py`: none). Stored rules keep running, because the lifecycle worker is server-side; the `allure-reports` 30-day rule (docs/garage.md:201) is one. A stack that re-PUTs a lifecycle config with a read/write (non-owner) key will start getting 403. That code lives in stack repos, which I did not trace. See the comment below.
- **v2.5.0, recommended**: the new `[s3_api] public_endpoint`. It is optional, and the chart does not render it. Not adopting it is fine; `additionalTopLevelConfig` is the hook if it is ever wanted.
- **Chart (packaging) deltas**, mapped against `argocd/platform/garage.yaml` values:
  - `s3.api.bindAddr` / `s3.web.bindAddr` / `admin.apiBindAddr` default to the old literal ports, so the Services, containerPorts and `/health :3903` probe render the same.
  - `noClusterRole` defaults to false, so the ClusterRole is kept.
  - `singleNode` defaults to false, so `replicas: 3` and `replication_factor = 3` are unchanged.
  - `service.admin` is off by default.
  - The ServiceMonitor `nindent` fix only affects `tlsConfig`/`relabelings`, and we set neither.
  - The stray ingress `---` is gone (both ingresses are disabled here).
  - `command`/`args` values are declared upstream but no template reads them. Inert.
  - The `helm.sh/chart` + `app.kubernetes.io/version` labels move. No immutable field carries them: selectorLabels are name+instance only, and `volumeClaimTemplates` carry no labels.
  - Net live effect: the image tag (`docker.io/dxflrs/amd64_garage:v2.5.0`, which exists on Docker Hub, pushed 2026-10-24) plus label churn. That matches the class-20 row's dry-run note.
- **Local patches**: all five re-applied by the script. The `--verify` leg in `ci` asserts every one: minReadySeconds=300, the serve-s3 pod label but not in matchLabels, only `Service/garage` selecting on it, garage-init resources, and meta-rotate after garage-init.

## Known issues

I scanned the 50 newest open issues on git.deuxfleurs.fr/Deuxfleurs/garage on 2026-11-13, plus a `v2.5` search. These touch our usage:
- **#1600 — regression in 2.5.0**: `GetObjectTagging` from a read/write key now returns **403** (it was 501). Clients that tolerated 501 (Ansible `amazon.aws.s3_object`) break unless the key has owner. Nothing in this repo calls ObjectTagging (grepped). Stack-side clients are untraced.
- **#1578** — the lifecycle worker can wrongly delete a key re-written while a node was offline or snapshot-restored across midnight. This is pre-existing (not a v2.5 regression). It is relevant because meta-rotation seeds a pod from its own snapshot (VENDORED.md §Local patches) and `allure-reports` has an expiration rule. Context, not new with this bump.
- **#1592** — upstream's documented "restore a Garage snapshot" commands fail for LMDB. It reproduces on v2.5.0 and on v1.3.1, so it is not a regression. Our meta-rotate seed does its own copy and was proven live on 2026-09-09. Worth knowing before the snapshot `preflight` takes is ever used as a restore point.
- #1575 (data loss with *degraded* consistency): N/A, we run `consistent`. #1594/#1588/#1535 are SQLite/fjall: N/A, we run LMDB.

## Platform compatibility

- **Class: stateful chart, un-armed.** The four-heading read feeds the human gate, and auto-merge is already on (enabled by the operator).
- **Kubernetes v1.36.1 / Talos v1.14.1 / Cilium 1.20.4** (`/work/repo` CLAUDE.md generated block): the chart uses only `apps/v1`, `v1`, `rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1`, `monitoring.coreos.com/v1`. No API-version concern.
- **Procedure**: docs/garage.md §Upgrading wants `scripts/garage-upgrade.sh preflight` (table repair + a metadata snapshot on every node) *before* the merge, inside a declared window. I cannot see from here whether it ran. Given the one-way property, that snapshot is now the **only** way back.
- **Backup LXC (class 19)** is still `garage_version: v2.3.0` (`ansible/group_vars/garage_backup.yml`). Class 19 says it *follows* in-cluster, which matters more now that the move is one-way. Leaving it out of this PR is right.
- **Renovate batch**: siblings open are #3280 (prometheus-operator-crds v33). Unrelated; nothing shared.

## Gate change

1 changed under `scripts/`: `scripts/vendor-garage-chart.sh`, which is a CI gate (`argocd-validate-pins` `--verify` leg; `component-check` `--check`). The edit is the two pin lines only (`GARAGE_CHART_TAG`, `GARAGE_CHART_SHA`). No condition, pattern, exit path or skip switch moved. Every decision point is **equal**.
Gate-drift (CI run 43434668569):
- `(A) devbox run argocd-validate-pins → master's side FAIL(1), this PR's side PASS — DIFFERS`, with `✗ Chart.yaml appVersion 'v2.5.0' != GARAGE_CHART_TAG 'v2.3.0'`. This is the intended shape: the pin IS the data the gate compares the rebuilt chart against, and master's pin rejects the new content by design.
- `component-check → TIMEOUT / TIMEOUT — same`.
- `(B) no test file changed`.
No loosening.

## BLOCKING

**`docs/dependency-classes.yaml` (class 20, `revert:`) and `docs/garage.md` §Upgrading assert a rollback that v2.5.0 forbids.**

The class-20 `revert` cell (rendered into `docs/dependency-upgrades.md` row 20) says: *"Inside one major upstream keeps protocols and data structures, so reverting a minor is a roll back to the old binary."* §Upgrading says the same about protocols and data structures, and calls the `preflight` snapshot the restore point only "across a major".

The moment this merges, all three Garage pods run v2.5.0. A `git revert` of this commit, which is the class-20 rollback a human would reach for, puts v2.3.0 back on nodes that upstream says *must not* be downgraded. This is the platform's only object store: tofu state, every stack's buckets.

**Adaptation, docs-only, worker-authorable paths** (`docs/` is un-owned since the ADR-128 trial; CODEOWNERS L88 is commented out):
1. In `docs/dependency-classes.yaml` class 20 `revert:`, state that a minor can be one-way. v2.5.0 is: per its release notes, no downgrade after a node upgrades. For such a release the rollback is **not** `git revert` but a forward fix, or restoring `preflight`'s pre-upgrade metadata snapshot under the old binary (writes since are lost; a human decides). Tell the reader to check each release's notes for that line.
2. Regenerate the derived tables (`docs/dependency-upgrades.md` row 20 and `argocd/resources/github-exporter/dependency-coverage.json`) with the class-register generator.
3. In `docs/garage.md` §Upgrading, make the same correction in its first paragraph: compatibility *within a running mixed cluster* is upstream's promise; *downgrade* is not.

**Operator-lane (no container):** `.github/renovate-global.json`'s Garage MINOR rule description says "this is not a format risk"; it should carry the same no-downgrade caveat. `.github/` is codeowned, so the codeowner lands that line directly.

## Evidence

- Upstream release notes via the Forgejo API: `git.deuxfleurs.fr/api/v1/repos/Deuxfleurs/garage/releases/tags/{v2.4.0,v2.4.1,v2.5.0}`. The no-downgrade and lifecycle-owner lines are quoted from v2.5.0's body.
- Issues read: #1600, #1578, #1592 (bodies), plus the 50-newest open list.
- Diff read in full (`git diff master...HEAD`, 16 files). Templates checked against `argocd/platform/garage.yaml` valuesObject.
- CI run 43434668569 at the head's merge ref: `vendor-garage-chart --verify` all ✓; gate-drift block quoted above.
- Docker Hub tag `dxflrs/amd64_garage:v2.5.0` exists, last_updated 2026-10-24T15:26Z.
- Greps: no lifecycle or ObjectTagging callers in this repo. Kubernetes discovery is in use, so v2.4.0's #1526 would have hit us. Class-20 revert text: `docs/dependency-classes.yaml:309`.
- Unverified (stated, not inferred): whether `preflight` ran before auto-merge was enabled; stack-repo callers of `PutBucketLifecycle`/`GetObjectTagging` with non-owner keys.

Comments (not blocking): stack consumers that PUT lifecycle configs or call ObjectTagging with read/write keys will 403 on v2.5.0 (#1573, #1600). The S3 API is the ADR-158 kind-test surface, so a stack's kind test pinned at v2.5 would surface it.

**Verdict: APPROVED.** Round 2. Round 1 had one blocking finding: the docs promised that reverting a Garage minor rolls back to the old binary, and v2.5.0 forbids downgrade. Commit `f09abf04` fixes it. This is still an un-armed major and the app version moves, so the handoff parks it for a human merge.

## Upstream

appVersion: v2.3.0 → v2.5.0
chart 0.9.3 → 0.10.4, app v2.3.0 → v2.5.0. Both come from the vendored `Chart.yaml` at base and head; the chart is built from the git tag, so there is no index to read.

Releases crossed: v2.4.0, v2.4.1, v2.5.0. The full read is in my round-1 review and still holds. In short:
- **v2.4.0** panics on start under Kubernetes discovery (#1526), which this deployment uses. v2.4.1 fixes it and v2.5.0 includes the fix, so skipping straight to v2.5.0 is correct.
- **v2.5.0 forbids downgrade.** Once a node is upgraded it must not go back to an older version. Mixing v2.x versions in a running cluster is still fine. **The docs now say this:**
  - The class-20 `revert:` cell in `docs/dependency-classes.yaml:309` now says a minor CAN be one-way and names v2.5.0. For such a release the rollback is a forward fix or the `preflight` snapshot, not `git revert`, and a human decides. It also tells the reader to check each release's notes for the no-downgrade line.
  - `docs/garage.md` §Upgrading now says the same ("Compatibility is not reversibility"). Its `preflight` step now calls the snapshot the restore point "for a one-way release, and across a major", and says writes made after the snapshot are lost.
  - The generated copies are regenerated: `docs/dependency-upgrades.md` row 20 and its register row (now v2.5.0), and `dependency-coverage.json`. The kps 92.21.2 and loki 3.7.10 lines in that diff are the generator catching up with commits already in the merge-base (#3343, #3342), not scope creep.
- **v2.5.0 lifecycle calls (`(Put|Get|Delete)BucketLifecycle`) now need owner permission** (#1573). This repo makes no such calls (grepped). N/A here.
- **Chart packaging changes** (bindAddr values, `noClusterRole`, `singleNode`, `service.admin`, the ServiceMonitor indent fix, label churn): they render the same against `argocd/platform/garage.yaml`, apart from the image tag and labels. No immutable field moves. All five local patches are re-applied and asserted by `--verify`.

## Known issues

I scanned the 50 newest open issues on git.deuxfleurs.fr/Deuxfleurs/garage on 2026-11-13 (round 1; this round's push changes no code):
- #1600: a 2.5.0 regression. `GetObjectTagging` from a read/write key now returns 403 instead of 501. Nothing in this repo calls it. Stack repos are untraced.
- #1578 (the lifecycle worker can wrongly delete keys after a snapshot restore) and #1592 (upstream's LMDB snapshot-restore commands fail): both predate v2.5. They matter more now that the `preflight` snapshot is the documented way back from a one-way release. Context, not a blocker.
- #1575 (degraded consistency mode) and #1594/#1588/#1535 (SQLite/fjall backends): N/A. We run `consistent` on LMDB.

## Platform compatibility

- Kubernetes v1.36.1 / Talos v1.14.1 / Cilium 1.20.4: the chart uses only GA APIs (`apps/v1`, `v1`, `rbac/v1`, `monitoring.coreos.com/v1`).
- **Class 20, un-armed minor:** a human merges, running `scripts/garage-upgrade.sh preflight` before the merge and `verify` after (docs/garage.md §Upgrading). Because v2.5.0 is one-way, the `preflight` snapshot is the only way back. **Run preflight before merging.** I can't see from here whether it has run.
- The backup LXC (class 19) is still on v2.3.0. It follows this class and is correctly left out of this PR.

## Gate change

1 file changed under `scripts/`, and it is a CI gate: `scripts/vendor-garage-chart.sh` (read by `argocd-validate-pins --verify` and `component-check --check`). The diff is the two pin lines (`GARAGE_CHART_TAG`, `GARAGE_CHART_SHA`) and is unchanged since round 1. Every decision point is **equal**.

Gate-drift (CI run 43444404411):
- `(A) argocd-validate-pins → master's side FAIL(1), this PR's side PASS — DIFFERS`. Master fails with `✗ Chart.yaml appVersion 'v2.5.0' != GARAGE_CHART_TAG 'v2.3.0'`. This is intended: the pin is the data the gate checks against, so the old pin has to reject the new chart.
- `component-check → TIMEOUT / TIMEOUT — same`.
- `(B) no test file changed`.

No loosening.

## Evidence

- `git show f09abf04`: 4 files, docs and the generated tables only. The chart and the pins are untouched, as carrier issue #3347 asked.
- Grepped `docs/`, `.github/renovate-global.json`, `VENDORED.md` and `scripts/garage-upgrade.sh` for leftover "roll back to the old binary" / "not a format risk" claims. None remain in docs. The one left is in `.github/renovate-global.json:334` (below).
- CI run 43444404411 at `f09abf04`: success. That includes the `dependency-coverage --check` leg that proves the generated tables are current.
- Upstream notes and issues: the round-1 Forgejo API reads (releases/tags v2.4.0, v2.4.1, v2.5.0; issues #1600, #1578, #1592).
- Not verified by me: whether `preflight` ran, and whether stack repos call lifecycle or ObjectTagging with non-owner keys.

Comment, not blocking: stacks that PUT lifecycle configs or call ObjectTagging with read/write keys will get 403 on v2.5.0 (#1573, #1600).

Operator-lane (no container): the Garage MINOR rule description in `.github/renovate-global.json:334` still says a bump inside one major keeps protocols and data structures, i.e. it is not a format risk. It should carry the same no-downgrade caveat. `.github/` is codeowned, so the codeowner lands that line directly.

## Specs review
Verdict: APPROVE — mechanical: no specs path and no rule-test path in this diff — nothing for the specs gate to read; approved mechanically (ADR-155, the repo-wide count). Head f09abf046f17.
